deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a borrowing or reading list headed 'Auf der Bibliothek nachzusehen' ('to look up in the library'), almost certainly meaning the Göttingen University Library. It continues the year-by-year lists on the neighbouring pages (p. 30: 1828 and 1837; p. 32: 1830, 1831, 1833, 1834). The year heading here is '1829'. Above it, in lighter ink, are the notes 'Berzelius' and 'Thaer'; these look like later reminders.

The 1829 entries are:
- Schiller–Goethe correspondence, parts 1–5. This is the 1828–29 Cotta edition.
- Rehberg, Sämmtliche Schriften, vols. 1–4.
- Dan. Huber, 'Johann Heinrich Lambert nach seinem Leben und Wirken' (Basel 1829).
- Herbart, Allgemeine Metaphysik, parts 1–2 (1828–29).
- Röding (reading uncertain), a book on the South American independence struggle, 1830, octavo.
- Klüber on the coinage of Germany, 1828, octavo.
- A geographical description ('Erdbeschreibung', reading uncertain) of East Frisia and Jever, 1828.
- A work on double-entry bookkeeping in agriculture.
- Legendre, Traité des fonctions elliptiques, tome 3, supplement 1. This is the 1828–29 supplement reporting on the new Abel–Jacobi theory of elliptic functions.
- Cuvier, Discours sur les révolutions de la surface du globe, 5th edition.
- Berzelius, Traité de chimie (Paris), tomes 1 and 6–8.
- Memorie della Reale Accademia delle Scienze di Torino, tomes 29–31.

Two later entries follow:
- Eduard Vehse, Tafeln der Geschichte, instalments 9–12, Dresden, Grimmer, folio (1838?).
- Transactions of the Royal Irish Academy, vol. 19, Dublin, 1843 (or possibly 1847), with Gauss's note '(Hamilton on equ. of 5 d)'.

That note refers to W. R. Hamilton's work on the quintic, i.e. his examination of Abel's impossibility argument and of Jerrard's claimed method for solving equations of the fifth degree. It shows Gauss's continuing interest in the solvability of the quintic and in the Abel–Jacobi developments. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: Possible citation slip by Gauss. Hamilton's long paper on Abel's argument ('On the argument of Abel...', Trans. RIA vol. 18, 1839) appeared in vol. 18, not vol. 19. His Jerrard inquiry appeared in the British Association Report for 1836. Either Gauss mis-cited the volume, or vol. 19 contains a further Hamilton piece on the quintic. This is unsure and needs checking against the Trans. RIA contents.

results.what: Library reading list. It includes Legendre's Traité des fonctions elliptiques, vol. 3, supplement 1, and Hamilton's work on equations of the fifth degree in the Trans. Royal Irish Academy.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a book and borrowing list with no mathematics. Gauss's interest in Legendre's supplements and in the Abel/Jacobi and quintic literature is well documented.
transcription_corrections: 'Due[?] Jebbs[?], Lambert nach s. Leben u. Werken' should read 'Dan. Huber, Lambert nach s. Leben u. Wirken'. This is Daniel Huber, Johann Heinrich Lambert nach seinem Leben und Wirken, Basel 1829.
'Albert Ortsbeschreibungen' more likely reads '... Erdbeschreibungen von Ostfriesland u. Jever 1828'. The author's name is uncertain.
'Röding Süd Amerikanische freiheitskampf' is probably 'Süd-Amerikanischer Freiheitskampf'. The author's name is uncertain.
'Beckmann[?]' (the bookkeeping author) is uncertain from the image.
The final date may be read as 1843 or 1847. The last digit is ambiguous in the image.
'Roial' is Gauss's own spelling of 'Royal' and is not a transcription error.
